title: I built a pixel-art open-world shooter in 24 hours using ONLY Gemini 3.0 Pro (Code + Art). Here is my workflow.
author: uskyeeeee
selftext:
Hi everyone!

I still can't quite believe it, but in just one day, I managed to build the open-world pixel game I've always wanted. It features shooting, driving, building, and a fully destructible environment.

The craziest part? I used Gemini 3.0 Pro for everything. Not just for the game logic, but for the pixel art too (programmatically drawn, no image generation models used). Honestly, the development process was so fluid it felt more like playing a game than coding one.

Here is the breakdown of my tech stack and workflow:

🛠️ The Tech Stack: Vanilla JS + Canvas I explicitly chose NOT to use any complex game frameworks (like Phaser or Unity).

\- Reasoning: For an AI in this context, frameworks can often become bloat/overhead. Vanilla JS is clean, token-efficient, and easier for the LLM to manage in a single context window.

📚 The Workflow: Documentation is King This was my secret weapon. I didn't just ask for code; I wrote heavy documentation.

\- I created SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) for every component.

\- Before writing code, I establish the "rules" in markdown.

\- This prevents the AI from hallucinating different coding styles and drastically reduces rework.

🎨 The Art: "Coding" the Pixels I didn't use Midjourney or DALL-E. I asked Gemini to write the Canvas API code to draw 32x32 pixel sprites.

\- The Challenge: Getting complex animations (like an 8-frame walk cycle) is tough for an LLM.

\- The Result: It took a few tries to get the proportions right, but it actually works! It feels like magic seeing code turn into a cute character.

🎮 Current State & The Plan Right now, this is a technical demo with no real gameplay loop yet.

\- Implemented: Top-down shooting, Vehicle physics, Building system, Object destruction.

\- Goal: I plan to build one new system every day to push the limits of what AI can handle in a persistent project.

It’s a bit rough around the edges, but it’s the most complete game I’ve ever made using pure AI.

I’d love to hear your thoughts or answer questions about the prompting workflow!

comments.author: Slackluster
comments.body:
Nice writeup, you should post a link to the game!

For your next game you could try LittleJS Engine, it is a free and open source JS game engine with a comprehensive feature set and super fast WebGL sprite rendering. I have been working on improving how well it interfaces with AI. It would really help to get feedback from other devs who try it.

There are 2 big advantages here. The engine code is already written so the AI can focus on just the game part of things. Also using 2dCanvas will get very slow when you push the limits, switching to LittleJS will allow orders of magnitude more sprites.

* [LittleJS Engine](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS) \- GitHub Repo, just passed 4000 stars!
* [LittleJS AI Experiments](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS-AI) \- Templates and prompts for AI assisted development.

replies.author: Unfair_Ad_2157
replies.body: This is awesome, can you explain to me how I can develop a small game with this and AI? I have to tell to gemini or so that I want to use littleJS for graphics and code and later on? How to try it?

replies.author: Slackluster
replies.body:
The best way to use AI with LittleJS is to [download the latest LittleJS release.](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS/releases/tag/v1.18.0) Unzip that file and point the AI at that folder. I recommend VS code with Copilot. Then just ask the AI to make a very test simple game as a quick experiment and see if it works. The AI should be able to figure it all out.

Another easier but not as good option is to use Gemini or ChatGPT directly. Gemini is not a great option because you can not run games directly inside Gemini, so you need to save and open in web browser. ChatGPT is much easier because you can run the games inside ChatGPT and if there is a bug, just click the fix bug button, but still not as good as Copilot with Claude.

* [LittleJS Gem for Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/gem/53f8957f46c5/abf923743afdba74)
* [LittleJS GPT for ChatGpt](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-67c7c080b5bc81919736bc8815836be6-littlejs-game-maker)

comments.author: TheKaleKing
comments.body:
This is really cool, well done! In one day?! This is crazy. I've been using AI for a while but I don't think I could've gotten all that done in a day.

What do you mean by this:  I created SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) for every component.  
Does that mean like comment headers in every script?

Can you explain a bit more about how you generated animations with LLM? From my understanding you used gemini to write some code that then you could call to generate animations?

Did you make a huge plan before starting? LIke brainstorming with the LLM to make a step-by-step plan or no?

How did you do to maintain a consisten art style? That's one of my biggest problem. I make a "art-style-guide.md" which I brainstomr with LLM and then I give that to every LLM before generatnig an asset like "generate a duck following the given artstyle doc" but it doesn't always work that great.

Also did you experience both with and without a framework and it's why you didn't go with a framework on this project? I usually work with unity but I found AI wasn't THAT great at writing unity code so I tried phaser js for this new little game I'm working on and it seems better. It seems like logically using a framework would make it a bit easier for AI to write stuff faster but I haven't tried without a framework at all.

This is really cool stuff man, well done! Share your game, I'd love to play it.

I'm working on a phaser game myself just for fun, and I already got it accepted on the google play store (free without ads). The app version was just the early build, now I'm actually making it better, and the goal is to send an update next week and be done with it. It's more of a for fun project, and just to have something on the app store, and an AI experiment but I'm having so much fun. Sharing if you want to check it out: [https://nose-dive.vercel.app/](https://nose-dive.vercel.app/)

I love planes so you're flying a boeing 747 and then you can "collect" other planes for XP and then you need to avoid all the birds. It's all over the place honestly not as polished as your game but having a lot of fun!
